subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw implement this as diagnostics-only visibility first, or add a default-off strict inheritance mode that fails closed when configured tools are clipped?
rationale: The remaining work changes security policy semantics and user-visible tool availability, and automation cannot choose the permanent default or compatibility posture safely.

options.title: Diagnostics first
options.body: Expose declared/effective/removed tools and blocking layers without changing runtime clipping behavior, then evaluate strict parity from observed diagnostics.

options.title: Opt-in strict mode now
options.body: Add a new explicit config setting that fails closed on tool clipping, with fresh-install and upgrade proof for both default and strict behavior.

options.title: Keep current clipping only
options.body: Treat the existing effective inventory and audit logs as sufficient and close future strict-mode work as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics first
recommendation.body: Expose declared/effective/removed tools and blocking layers without changing runtime clipping behavior, then evaluate strict parity from observed diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent capability-profile refactor is the central adjacent ownership signal for deciding whether strict tool policy should become a runtime contract.
